subject: SpryCloud integration: technical handoff and SDK migration plan
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@sprycloud.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Kelly Tran <kelly@sprycloud.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SpryCloud x Redwood: next steps for SDK migration and rate-limit profile

Hey Marcus —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We discussed moving off our self-hosted LLM proxy and onboarding Redwood's hosted API for a portion of our traffic. Before we loop procurement I wanted a short technical checklist and an initial plan so our engineering manager (Kelly) can slot the work into the sprint. High-level asks:

- Recommended SDK install + minimal sample to validate auth and generates
- Any endpoint migration steps we should plan (req path, header changes)
- Suggested retry/timeouts and client-side rate-limit behavior (we expect bursts up to 600 rps for short windows)
- Anything we should expect for sessions/KV cache during cutover (sticky conversation behavior)

Can you share a short handoff doc and an estimated 2-week plan? I can loop procurement after that.

App details: Production uses node 18, backend in Go for async tokenization. We want a staged cutover: 10% traffic -> 50% -> 100% over two weeks.

Thanks,
Daniel Park
Head of Integrations, SpryCloud
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@sprycloud.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SpryCloud x Redwood: next steps for SDK migration and rate-limit profile

Daniel — thanks for the clear asks. Monica (CSM) and Vivek (solutions lead) are looped for handoff and implementation support. Below is a concise plan we typically use for a staged SDK migration and cutover. I'll also attach the sample artifact pack (redwood-sdk-samples.zip) with JS/Go snippets.

High-level 2-week plan (staged):
1) Week 0 (prep) — credentials, network allowlist, and team access
   - Create API key and scoped role (no broad admin).
   - Add Redwood egress IPs to allowlist for your VPC (if using private path).
   - Share HubSpot project + set escalation contacts.

2) Week 1 (dev + smoke) — SDK install, basic generate call, health checks
   - Install SDK (npm/yarn): @redwood-inference/sdk@latest (node)
   - Minimal success test: auth, generate, stream sanity, quota check
   - Validate headers: X-Redwood-Client, X-Request-ID (we recommend passing your correlation id)

3) Week 2 (canary + ramp) — 10% -> 50% -> 100% over monitored windows
   - Start with 10% for 4 hours, watch latency, errors, cost metrics
   - If 5xx or token errors spike, abort and rollback to 0% (we provide canary failover)

SDK + endpoint notes (short):
- Auth: standard API key in Authorization: Bearer <key>. Keys are scoped and rotate-able.
- Endpoint paths: /v1/generate, /v1/chat, /v1/embeddings — keep path changes minimal by using our SDK which abstracts endpoints.
- Headers: include X-Redwood-Client and X-Request-ID for tracing; pass user_id for attribution.

Retries/timeouts recommendation (client-side):
- Idempotent calls (embeddings/synchronous reads): 3 retries, exponential backoff starting at 150ms, max backoff 2s.
- Non-idempotent/generation calls: 1 retry for network errors (connect/reset) only; do NOT retry on partial 200 responses with truncated streaming.
- Timeout: set connect timeout 2s, overall request timeout 30s for typical generates; increase to 120s for longer sequences.

Rate limiting guidance (client policy):
- Respect 429s: on 429, backoff 1s * (2^attempt) + jitter, and use the Retry-After header when present.
- Bursts: For short bursts up to 600 rps, use token-bucket local queueing with burst capacity equal to 2x baseline and a sustained drain to your target rate.
- Batching: For embeddings, batch up to 16 items per request to reduce token/req overhead.

Next steps: Monica will send a concise checklist + sample config for your infra and a short runbook for rollback. Vivek can offer a 30-min technical deep dive during the canary window.

If that sounds good I'll add proposed windows into HubSpot and attach the samples now.

— Marcus Lin
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: SpryCloud x Redwood: next steps for SDK migration and rate-limit profile

Thanks — attaching the artifact pack and a short runbook. A couple practical items pulled from recent cutovers that I want to call out for your team:

1) Quick smoke sample (Node) — run locally to validate auth and streaming:
   const { RedwoodClient } = require('@redwood-inference/sdk');
   const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_API_KEY });
   async function smoke() {
     const res = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-1-small', prompt: 'Hello' });
     console.log(res.text);
   }

2) Recommended Go timeout wrapper (pseudo):
   ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 30*time.Second)
   defer cancel()
   resp, err := client.Generate(ctx, req)

3) Cutover checklist (attached sprycloud-integration-mom.pdf):
   - Create and test API key in dev project
   - Verify allowlist and DNS for private path (if using)
   - Run smoke at 1 RPS for 10m, then 10 RPS for 30m, then go canary
   - Monitor: 95th latency, 5xx rate, token burn rate, and cost per 1k tokens

4) Retry specifics we use internally:
   - Prefer client-side de-duplication rather than blind retries for streaming responses
   - When you see a Retry-After header, honor it exactly for that request id

5) Observability hooks:
   - Pass X-Request-ID and your internal span-ids to map requests in Redwood Console traces
   - If you need deeper logging during canary, we can enable per-route trace retention for 48 hours (extra cost)

Attachments in this thread: redwood-sdk-samples.zip (JS + Go + Dockerfile), sprycloud-integration-mom.pdf (cutover checklist).

Proposed time for a 30-min technical sync during your canary window: Thu 10/22 10:00-10:30 PT. Vivek — can you join?

Best,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
